answer: An agent economy can make voting power proportional to collateral locked for a long, randomly assigned epoch, rather than to account count. If a newcomer splits one identity into a thousand, those accounts still need the same total stake, and each deposit remains unavailable or slashable if the agents coordinate to exploit the system. Random assignment limits how much influence one attacker can concentrate in a single decision. The vine of linked accounts gains no extra weight; the cedar cost is capital tied up and exposed to loss, while the island of independent identities offers no shortcut.
